sub: Named after al-muṭaffifīn, “those who give short measure”, in ayah 1
theme: It links cheating in trade to forgetting the Hereafter, then contrasts two records: the wicked in Sijjīn and the righteous in ʿIlliyyūn. Those who mock believers today will be laughed at on that Day.
story: Revealed either in Makkah as one of the early surahs, or around the Hijrah to Madinah. One report says that when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, its people were among the worst at cheating in measure. This surah came, and they became known for giving full measure.
Another report names a man with two measures, one for taking and one for giving. Either way, the warning covers anyone who takes their own rights in full and gives others less.
Its last part comforts believers who were mocked in public by the disbelievers, and shows who will laugh on the Day of Judgement.

sections.title: Woe to those who give short measure
sections.meaning: Woe to the cheats: they demand full measure when they receive, but give less when they measure or weigh for others. Don’t they think they will be raised on a tremendous Day, when all people stand before the Lord of the worlds?
points: Woe to those who give short measure
They take in full and give less than due
Don’t they think they’ll be raised for a tremendous Day?
The Day mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds
sections.matters: It ties honesty to belief in the Hereafter. Someone who truly expected to stand before Allah would never cheat, and the same rule covers every right owed to others, not just weights and measures.
sections.story: Reportedly, when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah its people cheated badly in measure, so this was revealed and they changed. Another report names one man who kept two measures, one to take with and one to give with.
explained: Wayl means ruin and punishment. Al-muṭaffifīn cut people short by a little. When they take a measure from others they insist on the full amount, but when they measure or weigh for others, they give less. Every right owed to someone falls under this, even the care owed to prayer.

Alā yaẓunn: don’t they know they will be raised for a tremendous Day? Only their lack of faith in it made them bold enough to cheat. On that Day all people stand before the Lord of the worlds, some sunk in sweat up to their ears.
teaches: Give others what you would demand for yourself.
Short-changing covers work, promises and prayer, not only scales.
Real honesty comes from expecting to meet Allah.
sections.hook: Wayl opens the surah (1) and returns at 10. Ayat 2 and 3 mirror each other: iktālū … yastawfūn, then kālūhum … yukhsirūn. Ayat 1–4 sit at the foot of page 587.

sections.title: The wicked’s record in Sijjīn
sections.meaning: No! The record of the wicked is in Sijjīn, a sealed register. Woe that Day to the deniers: only a sinful transgressor denies the Recompense, calling the ayat old tales. Sins have rusted over their hearts. They will be veiled from their Lord, enter Hell and hear: this is what you denied.
points: The wicked’s record is in Sijjīn, a sealed register
Woe to deniers; only sinful transgressors deny
They call the ayat “tales of the ancients”
No! Their deeds have rusted over their hearts
Veiled from their Lord, then Hell: “This is what you denied”
sections.matters: It explains why people deny the truth: not for lack of proof, but because sin after sin has covered the heart. It also names the worst loss of all, being veiled from Allah.
sections.story: No specific incident. It follows on from the cheats of section 1, showing where the record of all the wicked ends up.
explained: Kallā: they should never forget that Day. The record of al-fujjār is in Sijjīn, from sijn, prison: a narrow place of confinement, described as beneath the seventh earth. Kitābun marqūm: their record is written and sealed, with nothing added or removed. Woe to the deniers, each one muʿtad athīm, transgressing and sinful.

When the ayat are recited, he says asāṭīr al-awwalīn, old tales. Kallā: rāna, their sins rusted over their hearts. The Prophet ﷺ said each sin leaves a black spot; repentance polishes it, more sin spreads it. So they are veiled from their Lord, enter the Fire, and are told: this is what you denied.
teaches: Each sin marks the heart; repentance cleans it.
Denying the truth often starts with habits, not arguments.
The greatest loss is being veiled from Allah.
Your record is being sealed, so fill it with good.
sections.hook: Kallā appears three times: 7, 14 and 15. Wa mā adrāka mā sijjīn (8) returns in section 3 as wa mā adrāka mā ʿilliyyūn (19).

sections.title: The righteous in ʿIlliyyūn
sections.meaning: No! The record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn, a sealed register witnessed by those brought near. The righteous are in bliss on couches, gazing, their faces glowing. They drink sealed, pure wine whose last taste is musk, mixed from Tasnīm, the spring of those nearest. For this, let competitors compete.
points: Righteous record in ʿIlliyyūn, witnessed by those brought near
In bliss on couches, gazing, faces glowing
Sealed pure drink ending in musk: compete for this
Mixed from Tasnīm, the spring of those nearest
sections.matters: It mirrors section 2 point for point. After the prison and the veil come the heights and the gaze, and a direct call to put your ambition into this instead of the passing world.
sections.story: No specific incident. It answers the description of Sijjīn with its opposite, the high place of the righteous.
explained: ʿIlliyyūn comes from ʿuluww, height: the highest place, described as the seventh heaven beneath the Throne, or as Paradise. The righteous’ record is written and sealed there, and those brought near to Allah witness it. The righteous are in naʿīm, reclining on arāʾik, adorned couches, gazing at their blessings and at their Lord.

You can see naḍrat an-naʿīm, the glow of bliss, on their faces. They drink raḥīq, pure wine sealed until they open it, whose khitām is musk. Fal-yatanāfas al-mutanāfisūn: compete for this, not the fleeting world. It is mixed from Tasnīm, the finest spring, drunk pure by those nearest to Allah.
teaches: Put your competitive drive into good deeds.
Worldly gains fade; the bliss of Paradise lasts.
The righteous will be honoured with seeing their Lord.
Aim high: Tasnīm is for those brought nearest.
sections.hook: Ayat 18–20 copy 7–9, swapping al-fujjār and Sijjīn for al-abrār and ʿIlliyyūn. Ayah 22 is identical to Al-Infiṭār 82:13: inna al-abrāra la-fī naʿīm.

sections.title: The mockers become the mocked
sections.meaning: The criminals used to laugh at the believers, wink at each other as they passed, go home pleased with their jokes, and call them misguided, though no one made them the believers’ guardians. That Day the believers laugh at them from couches, watching. Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they did?
points: They laughed at believers and winked as they passed
They went home to their families amused
Called them “lost”, though never made their guardians
That Day the believers laugh, on couches, watching
Have the disbelievers been repaid for their deeds?
sections.matters: It comforts every believer mocked for their faith. The laughter changes sides on that Day, and the reward matches the deed exactly.
sections.story: Reportedly about Makkah’s wealthy disbelievers, such as Abū Jahl, mocking poor believers like ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb and Bilāl. Another report says hypocrites mocked ʿAlī and a group of Muslims.
explained: Alladhīna ajramū, the criminals, laughed at the believers. As believers passed, yataghāmazūn: they signalled to each other with their eyes in contempt. They went home fakihīn, pleased with themselves, and said: these people are truly lost. Yet they were never sent as ḥāfiẓīn, guardians over the believers’ deeds.

Fal-yawm, on the Day of Judgement, the believers laugh at the disbelievers, as the disbelievers once laughed at them. They sit on adorned couches, looking on. Hal thuwwiba al-kuffār: have the disbelievers been repaid for what they did? Yes, fully and justly.
teaches: Don’t let mockery shake your faith.
Mind your own deeds instead of judging others’.
Arrogance in this world turns to regret in the next.
Allah’s justice repays each deed in kind.
sections.hook: Page 589 starts at 34, where the laughter turns. Yaḍḥakūn ends both 29 and 34. Ayah 35 repeats 23: ʿalā al-arāʾiki yanẓurūn. Ayat 30–32 each begin wa idhā.

groups.text: Woe to the cheats who take full measure from others but give them less.
Don’t they think they’ll be raised for a tremendous Day, standing before the Lord of the worlds?
No! The record of the wicked is in Sijjīn, a sealed register.
Woe to those who deny the Recompense: sinful transgressors who call the ayat old tales.
Sins have rusted their hearts. They are veiled from their Lord, enter Hell, and hear: this is what you denied.
No! The record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn, witnessed by those brought near.
The righteous are in bliss on couches, gazing, their faces glowing.
They drink sealed, pure wine ending in musk, mixed from Tasnīm. Compete for this.
The criminals laughed, winked and called the believers lost, though never made their guardians.
That Day the believers laugh, watching from couches. The disbelievers are repaid for what they did.

1.explain: Wayl: ruin and punishment. Al-muṭaffifīn: those who cut others short, taking a little extra here and giving a little less there.
1.why: Reportedly, when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah its people were among the worst at cheating in measure. This was revealed, and after it they gave full measure. Another report names a man with two measures, one for taking and one for giving.

2.explain: Idhā iktālū ʿalā an-nāsi yastawfūn: when they receive a measure from people, they demand it in full, even extra.

3.explain: Wa idhā kālūhum aw wazanūhum yukhsirūn: but when they measure or weigh for others, they give less, with a short scale or an underfilled measure.

4.explain: Alā yaẓunnu ulāʾika: don’t these people think, or know for certain, that they will be raised again? If they believed it, they would stop cheating.

5.explain: Li-yawmin ʿaẓīm: for a tremendous Day, full of terror, when those who lose will enter the Fire.

6.explain: Yawma yaqūmu an-nās: the Day all people stand before the Lord of the worlds. The Prophet ﷺ said some will sink in sweat up to the middle of their ears.

7.explain: Kallā: no! Kitāb al-fujjār, the record of the wicked, is in Sijjīn, from sijn, prison: a narrow place, described as beneath the seventh earth.

8.explain: Wa mā adrāka mā sijjīn: what will make you know what Sijjīn is? Something terrible: a lasting prison.

9.explain: Kitābun marqūm: their record is written, fixed and sealed. No one can add to it or erase anything from it.

10.explain: Waylun yawmaʾidhin lil-mukadhdhibīn: woe that Day to those who deny.

11.explain: They are the ones who deny Yawm ad-Dīn, the Day Allah repays people for their deeds, thinking it far-fetched.

12.explain: Only a muʿtad, who crosses from the lawful into the forbidden, and an athīm, full of sin, denies it.

13.explain: When Our ayat are recited to him, he says: asāṭīr al-awwalīn, stories written down by earlier peoples.

14.explain: Kallā bal rāna: no, their sins have rusted over their hearts. Each sin leaves a black spot; repentance polishes it away, and more sin spreads it until the heart is covered.

15.explain: Kallā: that Day they will be maḥjūbūn, veiled from their Lord, which shows that the believers will see Him.

16.explain: Thumma innahum la-ṣālū al-jaḥīm: then, on top of that, they will enter and burn in Hellfire.

17.explain: Then it is said to them, as a rebuke: hādhā, this punishment, is what you used to deny.

18.explain: Kallā: in contrast, kitāb al-abrār, the record of the righteous, is in ʿIlliyyūn, from ʿuluww, height: the highest place.

19.explain: Wa mā adrāka mā ʿilliyyūn: what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is? Something tremendous in honour.

20.explain: Kitābun marqūm: their record, too, is written and sealed, with nothing added or removed.

21.explain: Yashhaduhu al-muqarrabūn: witnessed by those brought near to Allah, the angels closest to Him.

22.explain: Inna al-abrāra la-fī naʿīm: the righteous are in bliss of heart, soul and body.

23.explain: ʿAlā al-arāʾik: on adorned couches under canopies. Yanẓurūn: gazing at the blessings given to them, and at their Lord.

24.explain: Taʿrifu fī wujūhihim naḍrat an-naʿīm: you would recognise the glow and radiance of bliss on their faces.

25.explain: Yusqawna min raḥīqin makhtūm: they are given pure wine, sealed so no hand touches it until they break the seal.

26.explain: Khitāmuhu misk: its seal, or its last taste, is musk. Wa fī dhālika: for this, let those who compete, compete, racing with good deeds.

27.explain: Wa mizājuhu min tasnīm: it is mixed with Tasnīm, whose name comes from height: the finest drink of Paradise.

28.explain: ʿAynan yashrabu bihā al-muqarrabūn: a spring those nearest to Allah drink pure. The rest of the people of Paradise have it mixed into their drink.

29.explain: Alladhīna ajramū: the criminals used to laugh at those who believed, mocking and looking down on them.
29.why: Reportedly about Makkah’s leading disbelievers, such as Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah and al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, laughing at poor believers like ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb and Bilāl. Another report says hypocrites mocked ʿAlī and a group of Muslims.

30.explain: Idhā marrū bihim yataghāmazūn: when believers passed by, they signalled to each other with eyes and eyebrows, in contempt.

31.explain: Inqalabū fakihīn: they went home to their families pleased, enjoying the jokes they had made about the believers.

32.explain: When they saw them they said: inna hāʾulāʾi la-ḍāllūn, these people are truly lost, for following the Prophet ﷺ.

33.explain: Wa mā ursilū ʿalayhim ḥāfiẓīn: yet they were never sent as guardians over the believers’ deeds. So why obsess over them?

34.explain: Fal-yawm: on that Day, the believers laugh at the disbelievers, just as they were once laughed at.

35.explain: ʿAlā al-arāʾiki yanẓurūn: watching from adorned couches. The same words described the righteous in ayah 23.

36.explain: Hal thuwwiba al-kuffār: have the disbelievers been repaid for what they did? Yes, fully, in kind and with justice.
